key_insight: A standardized benchmark (PoseBench) reveals where current deep-learning protein–ligand docking and structure-prediction methods succeed and systematically where they fail, quantifying strengths in pose recovery but exposing limits in scoring, ligand flexibility handling, and generalization to novel targets.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of a comprehensive, standardized benchmark and failure-mode analysis for AI-based protein–ligand docking, enabling fair comparison and revealing practical weaknesses that hinder real-world drug-discovery workflows.
method: Introduce PoseBench: a curated, diverse benchmark dataset and evaluation protocol for protein–ligand docking and structure prediction.
Evaluate multiple state-of-the-art AI-based docking and structure-prediction methods across standardized metrics (pose accuracy, ranking/scoring, robustness to ligand/protein diversity).
Perform systematic failure-mode analysis to identify common error sources (e.g., ligand flexibility, binding-site conformational changes, scoring miscalibration).
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a clear, quantitative roadmap for improving docking models and prioritizing research (better scoring functions, handling of flexibility, domain generalization), accelerating reliable model development for drug discovery.
visual_elements: Schematic of PoseBench pipeline: dataset curation → standardized inputs → model predictions → unified evaluation metrics
Bar/boxplot comparison of pose-accuracy and scoring performance across evaluated models
Heatmap showing performance by target class / ligand complexity to highlight generalization gaps
Example ground-truth vs predicted binding poses (success and failure case) annotated with error sources
paper_title: Assessing the potential of deep learning for protein–ligand docking
paper_authors: Alex Morehead, Nabin Giri, Jian Liu, Pawan Neupane, Jianlin Cheng
